flags.detail: A strict single-entry screen requires the organiser to state that only one entry, no rebuy and no add-on are permitted. No official document retrieved states that. Venetian single-day structure sheets are silent on re-entry. Wynn, Bellagio, Caesars Palace and Wynn daily terms all state re-entry or rebuy rights explicitly. MGM Grand states neither.
flags.title: No event anywhere is confirmed single-entry by an official source

flags.detail: All 37 DSE IV structure sheets list buy-in allocation, late registration, starting chips and level length. None states whether a player may re-enter after elimination, except the multi-flight sheets, which state that a player who bags chips may not play a later flight. Absence of a prohibition is not a confirmation of single entry.
flags.title: Venetian structure sheets do not state a re-entry, rebuy or add-on policy

flags.detail: No official Venetian, Wynn, Bellagio, MGM Grand or Caesars page states a pedestrian walking time between a hotel tower and its poker room. Google/Apple Maps distances were not used because they are not official property sources. The 30-minute filter therefore cannot be applied to any row and remains empty.
flags.title: Zero verified walking times for any hotel-to-poker-room pair

flags.detail: A true nightly cost needs a dated quote for specific dates and occupancy. Only resort fees and one property's room-tax rate are published. All room-rate cells are blank; the trip estimator asks the user for a live rate rather than inventing one.
flags.title: No dated hotel checkout total for any property

flags.detail: Venetian hotel terms state a 13.38% Clark County Room Tax. Wynn, Bellagio and MGM Grand terms say taxes are estimated at current rates without printing a percentage. Applying 13.38% to those properties would be an inference, so the estimator applies it only to the Venetian.
flags.title: Venetian room tax is verified only for the Venetian; other properties' rates are unstated

flags.detail: The official poker page advertises 11 AM, 7 PM and 11 PM daily starts, but the linked schedule PDF is headed 'MGM Grand August Tournament Schedule' and lists 11:10 AM, 7:10 PM and 11:10 PM. The current applicability of those times is unconfirmed.
flags.title: MGM Grand weekly schedule PDF is titled August with no year

flags.detail: The $120 NLH structure allocates $92 to the prize pool, $13 house fee, $4 promotions, and a one-time voluntary $11 staff gratuity that grants 10,000 additional chips (15,000 + 10,000 = 25,000). That is money for an in-event advantage, so the event is excluded from the no-add-on group.
flags.title: MGM Grand $11 gratuity buys 10,000 extra chips

flags.detail: The poker room page and the series overview page both label the WPT Fall Festival (Oct 28 - Nov 15, 2026) as 'Current Series' and DeepStack Extravaganza IV (Nov 16 - Dec 23, 2026) as 'Next Series', although the DSE IV event page is live with results columns. Event facts were taken from the dedicated DSE IV schedule.
flags.title: Venetian series page still labels the previous series as 'Current Series'

flags.detail: In the official schedule PDF text, event 32's date cell renders as 'LIPS CHAMPIONSHIP CHAMPIES CHAMPIES CHAMPIES' rather than a date, and several row labels are truncated. Dates were taken from the HTML event page where the PDF row label was unusable; both agree elsewhere.
flags.title: Venetian schedule PDF text layer mislabels some date cells

flags.detail: The earliest start found in any official source is 09:10 AM (Venetian Event 46, Dec 12 turbo satellite). Wynn WPT Day 1As start at 10:00 AM (Super Gold Million, Dec 10-11). Caesars Palace's earliest daily event is 10:00 AM. An 08:00 AM start is not available in any retrieved official schedule.
flags.title: First verified start time is 09:10 AM; no 08:00 AM tournament exists

flags.detail: The Wynn poker page states the daily tournament schedule is suspended during each Wynn Signature, Wynn Millions and Classic tournament series. The WPT World Championship runs Nov 27 - Dec 21, 2026, which covers most of the Venetian festival window, so Wynn daily events should not be assumed to run then.
flags.title: Wynn daily tournaments are suspended during the WPT series

flags.detail: The official Horseshoe page states the Hall of Fame Poker Room runs '6 exciting tournament times daily' but no schedule, buy-in, guarantee or entry-limit document could be retrieved. The room is therefore listed as unverified with no event rows.
flags.title: Horseshoe Las Vegas publishes no retrievable tournament structure

questions.how: Ask the Venetian poker room (702.414.7657) or the tournament director for the written rules covering re-entry, rebuy and add-on for one-day DSE events; request it in writing.
questions.known: Wynn ($600/$400K, TORSE, PLO $400, daily Mon-Thu and Sat-Sun), Bellagio Friday $600, Caesars Palace dailies, Wynn Friday rebuy event and MGM Grand all permit re-entry, rebuys or a paid chip add-on by explicit official text.
questions.missing: A written official statement for any single event that only one entry is allowed. Venetian structure sheets are silent on this point.
questions.q: Is any event actually single-entry, no rebuy, no add-on?

questions.how: Pick the window; the site's date filter then shows only playable events. Rates and taxes are date-sensitive and nothing can be priced without them.
questions.known: The Venetian festival runs Nov 16 - Dec 23, 2026; the Wynn WPT series runs Nov 27 - Dec 21, 2026.
questions.missing: Arrival/departure dates, nights, occupancy and room type.
questions.q: What are the exact trip dates and how many nights?

questions.how: Run a dated booking query on the property's own site for the exact stay and enter the nightly rate into the trip estimator; keep the checkout total.
questions.known: Venetian: $55 resort fee plus tax per night, 13.38% Clark County room tax, $20/day guest self-parking, $150/night incidental hold. Wynn/Bellagio: $55 resort fee plus tax. MGM Grand: $50 resort fee plus tax.
questions.missing: A dated room rate for the chosen nights, and the room-tax percentage for Wynn, Bellagio and MGM Grand.
questions.q: What is the real all-in hotel cost per night?

questions.blocks: Same-day sequencing beyond a conditional fallback
questions.how: Estimate from structure only as a range; treat any same-day second entry as conditional. Ask the poker room for typical attendance.
questions.known: Level lengths, starting stack, break schedule and late-registration close for every Venetian event.
questions.missing: No official expected finish time or average field size for any event.
questions.q: How long does a one-day event actually run?

questions.how: Measure entrance-to-poker-room on site, or obtain a property-provided figure; do not substitute mapping-app estimates without labelling them non-official.
questions.known: Venetian poker room is in the Palazzo on level 2 of Grand Canal Shoppes; Wynn's is inside Encore; Bellagio's is north side of the casino next to the sportsbook.
questions.missing: Any official walking time or distance figure.
questions.q: What is the walking time from each hotel to its poker room?

questions.how: Recheck each room's own schedule page; the source monitor re-checks the pages on a schedule and logs changes.
questions.known: Earliest official start found: 09:10 AM (Venetian Event 46, Dec 12) and 10:00 AM (Caesars Palace daily, Wynn Super Gold Million Day 1A).
questions.missing: Any 08:00 AM tournament on the Strip in the window.
questions.q: Can the day start at 8:00 AM?

questions.blocks: Ranking on anything other than advertised guarantee
questions.how: Read guarantee ÷ entry fee as a description of the advertised floor only. Never treat it as expected value.
questions.known: Verifiable guarantees and the per-entry amount allocated to the prize pool, so guarantee-per-entry can be shown descriptively.
questions.missing: Field sizes; the guarantee is a floor, not a forecast.
questions.q: Which events have guaranteed prize pools that are comparable?

questions.how: Keep bounty, multi-flight, satellite and team events in separate labelled sections, as this site does.
questions.known: Several events pay part of the prize pool as bounties, and one series of $500K events is run across six starting flights.
questions.missing: Nothing structural; this is a presentation decision.
questions.q: Do bounty and multi-flight events belong in the same list?

questions.how: Call 866.255.8936 with code EPOKR25 for a dated quote and compare against the public rate for the same nights.
questions.known: Venetian publishes poker suite rates from $119 (Venetian) / $209 (Palazzo), conditional on six hours of live cash play or a $300+ tournament buy-in per night, otherwise the prevailing rate is charged.
questions.missing: Whether the chosen nights qualify, and the prevailing rate to compare against.
questions.q: Is a poker room rate available, and does it beat the public rate?

suggestions.decision: Send one email to each of the five poker rooms; publish the replies.
suggestions.title: Ask the card room for written entry rules before trusting any single-entry label
suggestions.why: Every single-entry claim on this site is blocked by the same gap: no organiser publishes an explicit one-entry-only rule. A written answer from the room unlocks the whole recommendation.

suggestions.decision: Accept the dated-log layout already used on the Hotels page.
suggestions.title: Buy the hotel rate as a dated log, not a number
suggestions.why: Rates move daily. A single stored value goes stale silently; a dated observation with a source link stays auditable.

suggestions.decision: Choose two date windows; enter their live rates in the estimator.
suggestions.title: Price two candidate weeks and compare like-for-like
suggestions.why: A trip-cost comparison is only meaningful for identical dates, nights and occupancy. Two candidate weeks would let you compare cost per tournament played.

suggestions.decision: Accept the primary-plus-conditional layout on the Day plan page.
suggestions.title: Treat any same-day second event as a conditional fallback, never a plan
suggestions.why: No official source publishes expected finish times. Committing to a 5:10 PM event after an 11:10 AM event assumes a bust that may not happen.

suggestions.title: Keep spend-advantage events in their own section, not deleted
suggestions.why: Rebuy, add-on and unlimited re-entry events are not bad value; they are bad for a fixed-budget comparison. Separating them keeps the comparison honest without hiding options.

suggestions.title: Label guarantee ÷ buy-in as a description, never as an edge
suggestions.why: A guarantee is a floor the organiser must pay, not an expectation. Showing it as a ratio invites over-reading it as a forecast.

suggestions.decision: Record Palazzo-to-Venetian-lobby and Venetian-to-Wynn times on the trip.
suggestions.title: Measure the two walks that matter, once, on foot
suggestions.why: The 30-minute filter cannot be applied from official sources because none states a walking time. Two on-site measurements would unblock the entire hotel filter.

suggestions.decision: Pick a primary objective; the day plan can then be rebuilt around it.
suggestions.title: Decide whether the trip is about volume or about one big event
suggestions.why: The best 'value' event and the best 'volume' schedule point in different directions: the $2,200 $1M Championship is the largest advertised pool, while the $200/$300 one-day events maximise entries per day.

suggestions.decision: Approve keeping the legacy pages as archived documents (current state) or removing them after review.
suggestions.title: Consolidate the four overlapping dashboards that earlier sessions left in the repo
suggestions.why: The repository currently publishes a root dashboard, a /docs subsite and a /verified subsite built by different sessions. Duplicate dashboards are the main source of contradiction risk.

suggestions.decision: Choose an alert destination (e.g. issue comment on this repo).
suggestions.title: Add a change-alert digest instead of relying on a page nobody reloads
suggestions.why: The source monitor records changes but nothing pushes them to you. A weekly digest of changed pages turns monitoring into a decision input.
